problems_found: A10 BR3 / P324 cond 7 violated: purging a LIGHT/ACTIVE case kept the WHOLE audit trail (case purpose, ticket, legal basis, hold reasons/requesters, every payload field) plus the full audit.jsonl mirror for audit_retention_days (possibly years). Only the minimal engagement audit may outlive retention_days (authorization ref, scope SHA-256, window, analyst, ledger). Verified with a probe: purpose text and hold reasons were still in the DB after the purge.

QuotaBook.quota_lines() crashed with ValueError (max() of an empty sequence) for any provider whose quota block declares only rate_per_second (urlscan, NVD, HIBP, gitlab, gleif, virusshare...) once it had deferred lookups or an expired signal. The engine catches the exception and drops every quota line of the case, which breaks P334 cond 7.

QuotaBook.defer() stored the free-text reason verbatim in a quota DB that may be team-shared. Module or provider messages that quote the entity value (for example an e-mail address) reached it, against the documented rule of 'pseudonymised deferrals only, never an investigated value'. The quota DB also ran without PRAGMA secure_delete, so purged deferrals were not overwritten.

Provider signals had no upper bound: a hostile or broken Retry-After or until value (years away) blocked a provider through the persisted signals table for years. ISO ends carrying non-UTC offsets were stored verbatim, which breaks the textual MAX() and pruning comparisons.

The token bucket ignored safety_margin: rates ran at 100% of the published limit (VirusTotal 4/min meant exactly 15 s spacing), against P334 cond 3 (at most 80%). The contract doc also wrongly claimed the HTTP client honours the returned wait: HttpClient._fetch discards the return value of quota.reserve(), so rate_per_second is not enforced at all.
write_reports built file names from case['case_id'] without validation. A crafted or damaged case id such as '../../x' wrote outside out_dir (path traversal) and created junk directories.
HttpCache.get() served rows older than cache_max_age_days between two daily prunes when the caller's ttl allowed it (A10 cap: defense in depth was missing).

hmacid accepted a secret.key owned by another user. A key planted in a shared or misconfigured V3LUM_HOME makes every pseudonym reversible by whoever wrote it. PSEUDONYMISED_TYPES also left SECRET_TYPES (JWT, card numbers, tokens) in clear in the case search index when a caller had not redacted them.

A cache or quota DB that could not be opened was silently ignored, and the report still claimed a complete purge. Re-purging an already purged case said 'not found'.

HostLimiter.acquire(opsec='active'): the first caller's pool size won, so a scope file's lower max_concurrency had no effect once another caller had created the host's pool. The documented behaviour was 'a lower max_concurrent lowers it further'.

ScopeTargets.url_match(..., exclusion=False) now requires a target prefix to hold for every variant. An exclusion matches any variant, case-insensitively, and /admin/ also covers /admin. Prefixes are stored canonical; a prefix with an encoded slash or backslash is a scope problem.
scope.py: ROE values naming V3LUM anywhere are refused.

tools.py: flags are compared by name in every spelling (-x, --x, -x=v, --x=v). '--' and '-' are refused. Module args may not set or override forced flags, the rate flag or the proxy flag (PolicyError 'policy').

http.py: new _Contact.credentials(). Credential headers (redact.is_credential_header) and configured secrets in a header, the URL or the body refuse LIGHT/ACTIVE requests. The scope's ROE header is exempt. This also applies on the legacy ScopedHttp path.
http.py: _identifying() matches 'v3lum' anywhere in the value.

http.py and net.py: ACTIVE contact without a scope is allowed only from an entity-less self-test context that has internal_seed, and then only to internal hosts. http.py: new _check_window(scope, clock, label), used by _Contact.request_rules and Connector._authorize (and therefore run_tool). Before window_start it raises PolicyError 'scope'; at or after window_end it raises Cancelled.

http.py: resolve_host never sends internal names to public resolvers. It uses Resolver(allow_public=False) on the default route, so only doh_internal answers, and refuses internal names on proxied profiles.

http.py: new shared _CancelWatch thread. It shuts down in-flight response bodies of cancelled runs (urllib3 HTTPResponse.shutdown) within about 100 ms. _read_body and _stream_body report a shut-down read as Cancelled, never as a complete body.

net.py: new Connector._tcp(), a non-blocking connect polled with select. A pending connect is abandoned within about 100 ms of cancel or the deadline. HTTP CONNECT uses a cancellable proxy connect plus short-timeout reads. SOCKS runs the PySocks handshake in a worker and shuts it down on cancel. Target names are never resolved locally on the direct route.
net.py: new _proxy_port() for scheme default ports (http 80, https 443), used by ensure_reachable and the CONNECT route. New _tcp_url() brackets IPv6 hosts in ledger URLs.

load_specs was not fault-isolated. Any one of these raised out of the loader and dropped every spec, bundled ones included, as 'spec:*': an invalid-UTF-8 spec file (UnicodeDecodeError), deeply nested JSON (RecursionError), an unhashable expected.json status (TypeError), or a huge integer in a numeric spec field (OverflowError inside validate_spec).
